paper.title: Provably and Practically Efficient Neural Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Neural contextual bandit with smooth activations (reward in NTK RKHS)
unmapped: Reward function lies in the RKHS of the neural tangent kernel of a fully connected net with activation sigma_s(u)=max(0,u)^s; the smoothness s of the activation determines the kernel
Contexts x_{t,a} for each of K arms revealed each round, chosen arbitrarily
settings.definition_quote: In the stochastic contextual bandit problem, at each discrete sequential step $t=1,2,\dots, T$, for each action $a\in[K]$, a context vector $\bfx_{t}\in \cX$ is revealed... receives the corresponding reward $r_{t} = h(\bfx_{t, a_t})+\xi_t$... (i) The input space is the $d$ dimensional hypersphere... (ii) The reward function $h$ belongs to the RKHS induced by the NT kernel, and $h(\bfx)\in [0, 1]$... (iii) $\xi_t$ are assumed to be conditionally $\nu$-sub-Gaussian

symbols.q_max: maximum batch size max_r q_r used for retraining the neural nets

conditions: Assumption 1: contexts on unit hypersphere S^{d-1}, h in NTK RKHS with h in [0,1], conditionally nu-sub-Gaussian noise
Assumption 2: NTK Gram matrix H >= lambda_0 I on all context-action pairs; f(x;W_0)=0
network width m >= poly(T, L, K, 1/lambda, 1/lambda_0, 1/S, log(1/delta))
tuning: fixed batch size q_r per group
number of training epochs J = Omega~(T), learning rate eta = O(1/T)

source.label: theorem:regret_guarantees
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass1} and \ref{ass2} hold. Consider NeuralGCB given in Algorithm~\ref{alg:NeuralGCB}, with $R$ neural nets, as defined in~\eqref{eq:nn} with $L$ hidden layers each of width $m \geq \text{poly}(T, L, K, \lambda^{-1}, \lambda_0^{-1}, S^{-1}, \log(1/\delta))$. Suppose NeuralGCB is run with a fixed batch size for each group, then the regret~defined in~\eqref{eq:regret_def} satisfies R(T) =\Oct( \sqrt{T \Gamma_k(T)} +  \sqrt{T \Gamma_k(T) \log(1/\delta)} +\max_rq_r\Gamma_k(T))

results.notes: Gamma_k(T) is the maximal information gain of the NT kernel (gamma_T). The theorem does not say 'with probability 1-delta' explicitly, but the bound depends on delta and the proof relies on high-probability confidence intervals, so it is recorded as high probability. The appendix also states an adaptive-batch bound O(sqrt(T Gamma log(1/delta)) max_r sqrt(q_r)) in prose only.

symbols.s_act: smoothness parameter s of the activation sigma_s(u)=max(0,u)^s (s=1 is ReLU)

conditions: uses information gain bounds of Vakili et al. (2021) for the NTK of sigma_s
tuning: batch size term does not dominate

source.label: theorem:regret_guarantees
source.quote: In particular, in Theorem~\ref{theorem:regret_guarantees}, we prove an $\Oct(T^{\frac{2d+2s-3}{2d+4s-4}})$ upper bound on regret, where $s$ is the smoothness parameter of the activation functions

results.notes: Explicit rate stated in the introduction as a consequence of Theorem 3 combined with the bound Gamma_k(T) = O~(T^{(d-1)/(d+2s-2)}). Not a formal statement itself.
